sources.title: ACA Health Rate Filings
sources.program: Individual and small-group commercial insurance markets
sources.scope_note: Re-verified live 2026-10-16: page text-identical to 2026-10-13 (2027 plan-year requested AND approved rate-change tables; 15 individual, 16 small-group companies; two-phase rate review text intact). New page-level observation 2026-10-16: request-to-approved divergence varies in direction — approved below requested (e.g., Ambetter Health of PA individual 40.90% -> 35.13%; Oscar individual 15.39% -> 1.38%), approved above requested (Health Partners Plans individual 15.90% -> 18.35%; Keystone Health Plan East individual 14.68% -> 15.98%; QCC Insurance individual 19.88% -> 21.31%), approved equal to requested (e.g., Independence Assurance small group 8.95% -> 8.95%), and '0.00% New Plan' rows with no prior premium to change (Ambetter Health Solutions of PA). Model discipline: encode the approved figure only; the request is neither a ceiling nor a floor; new-plan 0.00% rows are non-observations. Rate-change % and coverage-map links only: no premium amounts, no provider networks, no behavioral-health reimbursement figures. Market coverage area and premium filings do not prove a provider's network participation or behavioral-health reimbursement. Dated snapshot: docs/source-snapshots/aca-rate-filings-2026-10-16.md

sources.title: Eligibility Policy | Medicaid
sources.scope_note: Federal eligibility overview: mandatory vs optional eligibility groups; ACA expansion option (133% FPL); MAGI financial methodology (no asset test) with SSI-methodology exemptions for blindness/disability/age 65+ and 209(b) states; non-financial criteria (residency, citizenship/qualified non-citizen); coverage effective-date and 3-month retroactivity; medically needy spenddown (36 states + DC); fair-hearing appeals. No last-updated date displayed on page. Rules are state-administered and vary by state — page cannot establish any state's groups, limits, or expansion status. URL rot confirmed: /medicaid/eligibility 404s; /eligibility-policy is the canonical overview.
